Synopsis:
Climate warming is shifting boreal forests from evergreen-dominated to deciduous-dominated ecosystems. Disturbances (wildfires, storms), extended growing seasons, and increased soil nitrogen disproportionately favour deciduous trees. Modelling suggests this transition will reshape nearly one-third of global forest area, with material consequences for carbon, water, and energy cycles. Early data from Alaska and Canada indicate the shift is already occurring.
